exact_old_passage: Otherwise extend $f$ to the convex domain $[0,\infty)$ by its finite value $f(0)$. This extension is convex at the endpoint too: approximate a zero argument in any convexity inequality by positive arguments and pass to the limit using $f(0)=\lim_{t\downarrow0}f(t)$ from [F1].
exact_new_passage: If $f(0)$ is finite, extend $f$ to the convex domain $[0,\infty)$ by that value. This extension is convex at the endpoint too: approximate a zero argument in any convexity inequality by positive arguments and pass to the limit using $f(0)=\lim_{t\downarrow0}f(t)$ from [F1] and continuity at positive arguments from [F3]. If $f(0)=+\infty$, the excluded case shows that every index with $b_i>0$ has $a_i>0$, so all ratios used below lie in the original convex domain $(0,\infty)$.
